subject: Hospitality
title: Perishable Inventory Problem
description: A quick win: understand Perishable Inventory Problem.

hook.text: A hotel room is like a banana—if nobody buys it today, it's worthless tomorrow. This is the perishable inventory problem.

buildup.text: Unlike physical goods, hotel rooms can't be stored. Tonight's unsold room generates exactly zero revenue—it can't be sold.

discovery.text: Revenue managers must decide: sell cheap now to guarantee occupancy, or hold out for a higher-paying guest who might come later.

twist.text: Selling too cheap fills rooms but kills profit. Holding prices too high leaves rooms empty. The balance is where the art lives.

climax.text: Modern systems update prices every few minutes based on demand, competitor rates, and booking pace. It's automated chess.

punchline.text: Rooms expire at midnight. Revenue management fights the clock every day.

quiz.question: Why is hotel inventory considered 'perishable'?
options: Unsold rooms tonight generate zero revenue—they can't be sold tomorrow
